verdict.rationale: Increase's own webhooks documentation says it reaches out to your application when events occur. It also sends real-time webhooks for card authorization decisions, and a customer case study (Ramp) describes ingesting webhooks for each step of the transfer lifecycle. A List Events API serves as a polling fallback. The pack does not document how a subscription is actually registered, which keeps coverage partial. missing for 10: explicit documentation of registering webhook endpoints and choosing event types, signature verification and retry/delivery semantics, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: Increase can reach out to your application so that you can take action (such as sending an email alert about the transaction to your user) automatically.
we'll create a Real-Time Decision object in the API and send you a special real-time webhook.
If you don’t want to use webhooks, or if you need batch processing, you can also request Events from the Increase API using the List Events API.
ingest webhooks for each step in the transfer life-cycle
